verses.text: “Hear this, house of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel, and have come out of the waters of Judah. You swear by Yahweh’s name, and make mention of the God of Israel, but not in truth, nor in righteousness
(for they call themselves citizens of the holy city, and rely on the God of Israel; Yahweh of Armies is his name):
I have declared the former things from of old; yes, they went out of my mouth, and I revealed them. I did them suddenly, and they happened.
Because I knew that you are obstinate, and your neck is an iron sinew, and your brow brass;

therefore I have declared it to you from of old; before it came to pass I showed it to you; lest you should say, ‘My idol has done them, and my engraved image, and my molten image, has commanded them.’
You have heard it; see all this. And you, won’t you declare it? “I have shown you new things from this time, even hidden things, which you have not known.
They are created now, and not from of old; and before today you didn’t hear them; lest you should say, ‘Behold, I knew them.’
Yes, you didn’t hear; yes, you didn’t know; yes, from of old your ear was not opened: for I knew that you dealt very treacherously, and were called a transgressor from the womb.
For my name’s sake, I will defer my anger, and for my praise I hold it back for you, so that I don’t cut you off.
Behold, I have refined you, but not as silver. I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.
For my own sake, for my own sake, I will do it; for how would my name be profaned? I will not give my glory to another.
“Listen to me, O Jacob, and Israel my called: I am he; I am the first, I am also the last.
Yes, my hand has laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand has spread out the heavens. when I call to them, they stand up together.
“Assemble yourselves, all of you, and hear; who among them has declared these things? He whom Yahweh loves will do what he likes to Babylon, and his arm will be against the Chaldeans.
I, even I, have spoken; yes, I have called him. I have brought him, and he shall make his way prosperous.
“Come near to me and hear this: “From the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time that it happened, I was there.” Now the Lord Yahweh has sent me, with his Spirit.
Yahweh, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel says: “I am Yahweh your God, who teaches you to profit, who leads you by the way that you should go.
Oh that you had listened to my commandments! Then your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
Your offspring  also would have been as the sand, and the descendants of your body like its grains. His name would not be cut off nor destroyed from before me.”
Leave Babylon! Flee from the Chaldeans! With a voice of singing announce this, tell it even to the end of the earth: say, “Yahweh has redeemed his servant Jacob!”
They didn’t thirst when he led them through the deserts. He caused the waters to flow out of the rock for them. He split the rock also, and the waters gushed out.
“There is no peace”, says Yahweh, “for the wicked.”

footnotes.content: Notice how God speaks to those who *claim* His name but haven't claimed His way. He's not angry—He's clear-eyed about the gap between our words and our walk. Even when we swear by His name without truth, He doesn't abandon us; He calls us back to it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: How easy it is to name a city 'holy' and think the name makes it so. But God sees what we lean on—sometimes it's the place itself, not Him. Yet He keeps calling, because He loves us more than our false confidence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God shows His track record: 'I declared these things, and they happened.' It's not braggadocio—it's the voice of a Father who wants His children to know He's been faithful all along, so they can trust Him now in exile.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: An iron neck, a brass brow—stubborn resistance. God isn't scolding; He's naming reality with almost tender precision, the way you'd describe a beloved child's worst habit. He knows exactly what He's up against, and He loves them anyway.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God foresaw their idolatry and told them anyway. It's mercy wrapped in prophecy: 'When these things come true, you'll know your idols didn't do it.' He won't let them misremember Him, even when they're foolish.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After all this rebuke, notice the shift: 'Won't you declare it?' God invites them into His work. Yes, they've been blind and stubborn, but He's showing them new things and asking them to witness and speak. That's calling, not casting away.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hidden things, not from of old—God is doing something fresh. He's not recycling stale promises. In exile, when everything feels over, He whispers: 'I'm making something new, and you didn't predict it, so you'll have to trust Me.'
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Treachery from the womb—Jacob's whole story. Yet God doesn't give up on him. There's almost resignation in His voice: 'I knew this about you from the start, so I'm not surprised.' But He's still speaking, still inviting rescue.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: For my name's sake, I hold back my anger. What a phrase. God's restraint isn't weakness—it's an act of His own self-respect. His name is worth more to Him than His fury. That's why He defers cutting them off.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Not refined as silver, but chosen in the furnace—there's a difference. Silver is refined to make it precious; Jacob is refined because he's already chosen. The fire isn't punishment for the worthless; it's love's way of making the loved one pure.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'For my own sake'—God acts to protect His own name, not to owe anyone a debt. But this isn't selfish; it means His honor and our salvation are bound together. When He saves us, He saves His reputation too.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I am he; I am the first, I am also the last—the God of all time speaks to people in the middle of it. When you're in exile and everything feels random, this word anchors you: the One who sees all of history holds your hour too.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His hand laid the earth's foundation; His right hand spread the heavens. Then He calls them, and they obey. There's a line drawn from cosmic power to personal care: the God big enough to make the universe is near enough to call you by name.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Assemble and hear—God summons a council. The one He loves will do His pleasure against Babylon. This isn't opaque politics; God's showing them the shape of history. Cyrus is coming, named before he knew his own name, because God sees and guides.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I have called him, brought him, and he shall prosper—the clarity here must have been staggering in exile. God isn't hoping Cyrus will cooperate; He's arranged it. Your deliverance is already on the way.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From the beginning I have not spoken in secret; I was there when it happened—God's openness is His character. He doesn't hide His plans; He speaks them plain. And notice: 'The Lord Yahweh has sent me, with his Spirit.' The voice of the Servant echoes here—a shadow of One yet to come.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Your Redeemer teaches you to profit and leads you in the way you should go—not as a slave-master, but as a Father who wants you to flourish. What a gentle summary of salvation: rescue *and* guidance, *and* blessing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Oh that you had listened! The sorrow in this word cuts deep. Peace like a river, righteousness like ocean waves—the blessings they could have had. Not threats, but the ache of a God watching His people miss the gift He held out.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Descendants like sand, name never cut off—what God promises through disobedience's lament. It's the blessing stated *because* it was lost, a mercy whispered: even now, if you turn, that abundance waits.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Leave Babylon! Flee with a voice of singing—the call isn't quiet or shameful. Shout it: Yahweh has redeemed His servant Jacob. After all the rebuke, comes the exodus shout. That's how God ends a exile: not with apology, but with a song.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Through deserts, He made water spring from rock. The old story—Exodus remembered in exile—becomes the promise of the new journey. The God who carved rivers in wilderness before will do it again. He's faithful in pattern.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: There is no peace for the wicked. Readers today hear an echo in this hard word: we long for peace apart from God and find only restlessness. But we also know what comes next in the gospel—One who offers peace to the broken, mercy to the wicked-hearted who turn. Isaiah's closing 'no' opens the way for Jesus's 'yes.'
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
